item.research_question: How does the addition of scandium (Sc) to the equimolar Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloy system affect its crystal structure, microstructure, and superconducting properties?
item.material_system: Equimolar Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloys (nine alloys: five 4-component, three 5-component, one 6-component)
item.processing_route: Arc melting in an Ar atmosphere; ingots remelted several times and cooled naturally to as-cast state
item.test_conditions: Electrical resistivity (0.35–300 K, 0–9 T), specific heat (0.35–8.5 K, 0–9 T), magnetic susceptibility (1.8–400 K, up to 7 T), XRD, SEM BSE, EDS
key_findings: Addition of Sc transforms the single-phase bcc structure of the parent Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr system into a two-phase structure containing bcc and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) phases.
The hcp phase absorbs practically all Sc, while the bcc phase remains Sc-poor and identical to the parent system's bcc phase.
Microstructure becomes highly inhomogeneous with large bcc dendrites (10–100 µm) that are homogeneous in the center but show a fine dispersion of sub-micron precipitates at the edges.
Interdendritic regions consist of a fine dispersion of bcc and hcp precipitates (10–100 nm) with hcp precipitates in the majority.
Superconducting transition temperatures (TCρ) range from 6.4 K to 8.4 K across the alloys.
The superconducting molar fraction (x) at T→0 ranges from 61% to 86%, correlating linearly with the bcc phase fraction.
The Sc-containing hcp phase fraction is non-superconducting, while the Sc-poor bcc phase fraction exhibits superconducting parameters identical to the parent Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys.
The superconducting phase is classified as a type II, BCS-like, 'dirty' superconductor.
item.mechanism: Scandium has strong repulsion to Nb and Ta (positive binary mixing enthalpies) and affinity for Zr, driving phase separation into Sc-poor bcc and Sc-rich hcp phases. The hcp phase is non-superconducting due to the presence of Sc, while the bcc phase retains the superconductivity of the parent system. The inhomogeneous microstructure arises from the clustering of elements with similar atomic radii and the phase separation driven by mixing enthalpies.
item.limitations: The authors state that mechanical properties and corrosion resistance were deferred to another study. Additionally, accurate chemical composition of the dark (hcp) phase could not be determined in interdendritic regions due to the fine dispersion of precipitates preventing reliable EDS analysis of individual phases.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the mechanical properties and corrosion resistance of the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys will be investigated in a separate study.
quotes: The addition of Sc produces a two-phase structure in the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys, with one phase being bcc and the other hexagonal close-packed (hcp).

Superconductivity of the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys originates from the bcc phase fraction, which demonstrates identical superconducting parameters as the bcc Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr parent alloys, while the Sc-containing hcp phase fraction is non-superconducting.
The graph is shown in Figure 9, where a clear linear correlation is observed, where larger bcc phase fraction correlates with larger x.
